title: Solstice Energy outbound & discovery scratchpad
content:
Notes to self: Solstice Energy (US regional renewables operator) looks like a good fit for Redwood Private or Dedicated. They have a small ML platform team (2 engs) and a larger product org running customer-facing forecasting + field ops tools. Hypothesis: they need predictable inference for on-device-like latency for remote field tools and want data isolation for regulator audits.

Account snapshot:
- Company: Solstice Energy (founded 2012) - regional renewable operator: wind + distributed solar + battery storage.
- HQ: Denver, CO
- Key pain areas (public filings + job posts): forecasting accuracy, edge/field tooling for maintenance crews, compliance records for interconnect/regulators.
- Tech footprint: AWS, some on-prem control centers, using PyTorch/TensorFlow, internal feature store, Kafka for telemetry.

Primary contacts (from LinkedIn + intro thread):
- Priya Desai — Head of Digital Operations (primary sponsor) — email: priya@solstice.com — likely to care about reliability and compliance.
- Marcus Huang — Lead ML Engineer (technical economic buyer) — email: marcus.h@solstice.com — will push on integration effort and throughput/cost.
- Elena Cortez — Director Field Ops (user champion) — field app latency + offline capabilities.

Top hypotheses to validate on first call:
1) They treat inference as "critical path" for field crew decisions (latency SLA ~<1000ms for certain flows).
2) They cannot send some telemetry to third-party cloud for compliance; need private deployment or VPC.
3) Throughput is moderate (200-800 requests/minute at peak) with large burstiness (storm events).
4) They will be price-sensitive vs building-in-house given GPU costs and ops friction.

Value prop bullets tailored to Solstice:
- Predictable latency under bursty workloads (Dedicated pools + autoscale + graceful degradation to cheaper variants).
- Private deployment option (VPC + audit logs) -> solves compliance + control plane separation.
- Cost controls: batching, KV caching for repeated prefixes (eg: forecast requests) + model quantization suggestions to meet field latency budgets.
- Operational: rollouts, per-route tracing, and fallback policies so field teams avoid downtime during storms.

Technical fit / integration checklist (questions to ask Marcus):
- What are the input/output shapes and token budget for inference flows? (short structured prompts, sometimes longer logs)
- Do you need strictly air-gapped on-prem? Or VPC with managed control plane is ok?
- Current model types: are you using foundation models for NLU/formatting or custom autoregressive models for time-series forecasting?
- Expected concurrency and burst patterns (daily baseline vs extreme events) + SLA for 95th/99th p99 latency.
- Any requirements for on-device runtime or local inference on tablets/phones?

Outbound sequence (initial touches):
1) Cold email (short, outcome-oriented). Draft below.
2) Follow-up + one-pager (send tailored one-pager referencing field use case).
3) Warm intro to Marcus with an ask for a technical 30-min scoping call + bring sample trace data.
4) Offer pilot: 6-week Private trial (small VPC + 2 dedicated instances) to demonstrate p99 latency and audit logs.

Draft cold email (first outreach) — keep <120 words:
Subject: Lowering inference ops and latency risk for Solstice field tools

Hi Priya — I’m Jordan from Redwood Inference. We help engineering teams run reliable, low-latency LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments (VPC/on‑prem), while cutting per‑token costs with intelligent batching and caching.

We’ve helped utilities and field-heavy operators reduce p99 inference latency and ship offline-ready assistants tied to compliance logs. If you’re open, I’d love 20 minutes to hear how you run forecasting/field inference today and show a short plan to validate with a small private pilot.

If yes, suggest Tue/Wed next week. Thanks — JP

Call opening script (30-minute technical scoping):
- 0-5m: quick intros, goal of call (scoping + decide pilot feasibility).
- 5-12m: Priya/Elena explain field workflow + concrete latency/cost pain.
- 12-20m: Marcus deep-dive: ask checklist above, current infra constraints, telemetry availability.
- 20-28m: Walk through Redwood architecture quick map: Private control plane, Dedicated GPU pools, Smart routing, Caching. Emphasize audit logs and deterministic rollouts.
- 28-30m: Confirm next steps: pilot scope, stakeholders, data access, NDA if needed.

Objection handling (common):
- "We already have a small infra team building inference": Response — acknowledge; pitch Redwood as ops & cost multiplier: reduces engineering time, avoids GPU procurement, provides autoscaling + SLAs. Offer TCO comparison numbers in follow-up.
- "Security/compliance concerns about third party": Response — highlight Private deployment model (customer VPC + optional on-prem + KMS/HSM integrations) and audit logs; offer security questionnaire + SOC2 docs + optional tech deep dive with security.
- "Cost — seems expensive compared to self-hosting": Response — ask for current cost baseline and show unit economics: batching + cache + quantization reduces per-token costs; Dedicated commitments lower unit price and remove hiring/ops overhead. Offer a short model-level cost simulation if they share traces.
- "Not ready to commit to pilot": Response — propose a low-effort proof: synthetic workload replay + demo environment, or 4-week exploratory with minimal engineering time.

Measurables for pilot success:
- Achieve target p99 latency for critical routes (goal: <900ms).
- Demonstrate correct audit log generation for sample flows (security acceptance).
- Show a 20–30% reduction in per-request operational cost vs current self-hosted baseline (or at least a credible plan).
- Team ramp time <3 weeks to get a working integration.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Pull any public filings or case studies of Solstice working with cloud providers (TBD).
- Ask Marcus if they have sample telemetry or anonymized request traces we can use for cost/latency sim.
- Prep a 1-page tailored pilot SOW: deliverables, timeline, acceptance criteria, cost.
- Security pack: pull SOC2 + Private deployment config doc + example contract redlines.

Quick reminders to self:
- Keep outreach concise and outcome focused (pilot, not product lecture).
- Bring up compliance early (Priya cares).
- Offer both Dedicated and Private options — they’ll decide by risk tolerance.
- Loop in Maya for pricing model and Liam for integration scoping after first positive reply.

Scratch notes end — will refine after first call.
